sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1975. South-Eastern Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 613-664. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only a phylum-wide generalisation (p.622): 'Some languages are tonal but stress is generally important and related to intonation which may be quite complex.' Nothing specific to Daga; Daga section (pp.641-642) is geographic/bibliographic and refers to Murane & Murane 1967, 1972 and Murane 1974.

sources.citation: Murane, Elizabeth. 1974. Daga Grammar: From Morpheme to Discourse. Summer Institute of Linguistics Publications in Linguistics and Related Fields 43. Norman: SIL of the University of Oklahoma. xvi+443 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 8706)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 2234.242)
sources.note: Nothing. Ch.1 'Morphophonemics' (p.5) gives only the phoneme inventory (13 C, 5 V) and allophones; the Introduction (p.1) states 'This paper describes only the grammatical hierarchy of Daga'. Whole book scanned and searched: the only prosodic remarks are sentence-level intonation (p.150: 'a sentence in Daga is marked by final falling intonation.. yes-no interrogative which has a rising intonation finally') and phonological-sentence boundaries in ch.6-7. No word-stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Murane, John & Elizabeth Murane (compilers). 2007 [data 1963-1977]. Daga - English dictionary. Ukarumpa: SIL PNG. 113 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 31076.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Introduction covers layout and abbreviations only; headwords carry no stress/accent marks; no statement on stress (two entries note syllabification, e.g. '<guam> is two syllables <gu-am>').

sources.citation: SIL PNG Branch. [data checked by Murane, May 1992; printed 2004; posted 2011]. Daga (Dimuga) Organised Phonology Data. 4 pp. manuscript. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 42246.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' is present but left completely empty; only syllable patterns (V, VV, VC, CV, CVV, CVC, CVVC) and segmental conventions follow. Silent on stress.

sources.note: The only dedicated Daga phonology publication; abstract states three degrees of vocoid syllabicity are contrastive and that 'an alternative analysis in terms of word accent is rejected' -- the body must describe Daga stress/accent phonetics and state whether accent is predictable. 8 pages; would settle the catalog entry.
